Hematologist

Role type: Contractor

Location: Remote, United States only

Commitment: Part-time, project-based

Compensation: $160–$180 USD per hour

About the role

micro1 is looking for experienced Hematologists to support a customer project focused on improving AI-generated clinical documentation.

In this role, you'll use your clinical expertise to evaluate AI-generated transcripts and medical notes from outpatient hematology encounters. Your feedback will help improve the accuracy, completeness, and clinical relevance of AI-assisted documentation.

What you'll do

  1. Review AI-generated transcripts of outpatient hematology visits for clinical accuracy, completeness, and clarity.
  2. Evaluate clinical documentation, including History of Present Illness (HPI), interval histories, and Assessment and Plans (A&Ps).
  3. Identify inaccuracies or missing details related to hematologic diagnoses, treatment plans, medication management, and laboratory findings.
  4. Assess documentation of blood disorders, including anemia, bleeding and clotting disorders, and hematologic malignancies.
  5. Review how clinical notes capture treatment responses, adverse effects, transfusion requirements, and follow-up care.
  6. Provide clear, actionable feedback to improve AI-generated clinical notes and EHR documentation.

Required qualifications

  1. MD, DO, or equivalent medical degree, with board certification or eligibility in Hematology.
  2. At least 2 years of recent outpatient hematology experience following fellowship.
  3. Strong clinical experience diagnosing and managing hematologic disorders, including treatment planning and longitudinal patient care.
  4. Proven ability to independently document HPIs, interval histories, and Assessment and Plans.
  5. Solid understanding of hematologic treatments, transfusion practices, anticoagulation management, and laboratory interpretation.
  6. Strong written communication skills and attention to clinical detail.
  7. Based in the United States.

Preferred qualifications

  1. Experience treating both malignant and non-malignant hematologic conditions, such as leukemia, lymphoma, anemia, sickle cell disease, and coagulation disorders.
  2. Familiarity with AI scribe technology, EHR documentation templates, medical chart review, or clinical annotation projects.

Application process

Candidates will complete an AI interview to assess their relevant clinical expertise and experience.

About micro1

micro1 is a data lab that connects professionals with opportunities to apply their expertise to customer projects. We work with specialists across fields such as engineering, finance, healthcare, and law to support AI labs and enterprises. Through our extended network, contributors bring their knowledge and judgment to projects with their own scope, requirements, and engagement terms.

Role Title: Hematology Physician

Role Type: Contractor

Location: United States, Remote

  2. Proficiency with electronic health records (EHR) and clinical documentation workflows.
  3. Deep familiarity with chemotherapy cycle management and hematologic malignancy care.
  4. Experience in crafting or reviewing patient histories, including histories of present illness and differential diagnosis.
  5. Strong attention to detail and ability to communicate complex concepts clearly in both written and spoken formats.
  6. Previous participation in clinical research, quality improvement, or AI/data-driven healthcare projects is a plus.
  7. Motivation to support innovative healthcare projects with real-world impact.

Vanguard Clinical, Inc. is a Contract Research Organization (CRO) headquartered in San Diego, CA. Our mission is to bring innovation to clinical trial execution through passion, transparency, co-active communication, and integrity, to facilitate the successful development of life-changing medicines and therapies.

We are experts in clinical trial operations with a focus on Clinical Trial Management, CRO/Vendor Oversight, Trial Master File Management, Clinical Monitoring, Quality Assurance, Data Management and Study Startup. Our unwavering integrity forms the foundation for our strong relationships both internally and as a partner to our Sponsor clients. Beginning with study development, we bring a “white glove service” approach to clinical trials. Our flexible approach and ongoing process development ensure efficiency and adequate resourcing, allowing us to respond rapidly to our clients’ needs as they evolve.

Our talented team is driven by passion and purpose, which has afforded us the opportunity to successfully lead clinical programs for pharmaceutical, medical device and biotechnology companies of all sizes in a variety of therapeutic areas. Our mission is to conduct clinical trials with outstanding quality on behalf of our clients to bring new drugs to market with the utmost integrity and confidence in the results.

Position Overview:

Reporting to the Director - Clinical Monitoring, primarily responsible for the management of clinical sites and monitoring of clinical data at assigned sites. The Clinical Research Associate (CRA) will execute monitoring responsibilities for clinical trials in Phases 1, 2, and 3, in accordance with ICH/GCP guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Prepares for and conducts site qualification, site initiation, interim, and closeout monitoring visits.
  • Main point of contact between assigned sites and Sponsor.
  • Conducts all monitoring with a strong focus on data integrity and patient safety, adhering to GCP protocol and sponsor requirements.
  • Delivers high quality and timely reports following each monitoring visit.
  • Completes and submits monitoring-related expense reports in accordance with the company and/or Client’s travel & expense guidelines.
  • Works with the Clinical Operations Manager to identify, escalate, and resolve issues at assigned clinical sites.
  • Maintains Trial Master File (TMF)/Electronic Trial Master File (eTMF) for assigned sites.
  • Manages query resolution process with clinical sites and data management groups.
  • Travel of up to 75% may be required, including globally.
  • Quarterly travel to San Diego headquarters required, if not residing locally.
  • Other work-related duties, special projects, and/or other functions, as required.

Experience & Skills:

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in a Clinical Trial Assistant or other supporting project role with high attention to detail (3+ years of clinical monitoring experience preferred).
  • Prior experience with oncological trials strongly preferred.
  • Self-motivation, flexibility, ability to establish and manage multiple priorities, and multi-task effectively to meet stated internal and external commitments.
  • Must exercise sound judgment and take initiative, be able to work independently with minimal supervision while producing accurate high quality and timely work.
  • Must be able to work effectively within a team environment (independently and collaboratively).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills including strong professional presentation skills (internal and external audiences).
  • Thorough knowledge and understanding of ICH/GCPs and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Solid computer skills, including working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel Outlook, etc.)
  • Understanding of current GCPs/ICH/FDA regulations and guidelines to assess compliance with applicable regulations and guidelines.

Education:

Bachelor of Science degree in a scientific discipline from an accredited college or university is strongly preferred. Other bachelor's degrees with relevant industry experience will be considered.

Compensation Range:

$90,000 - 130,000 annually + benefits package and annual performance bonus (Includes: health insurance, 401k retirement plan, and paid days off)

Make an Impact as a Senior Clinical Trial Manager at Worldwide


As a Senior Clinical Trial Manager, you will lead the delivery of critical clinical site management activities across studies and regions, helping ensure research is conducted with quality, efficiency, and compliance at every stage. Your leadership will directly support the successful execution of clinical trials and contribute to bringing new therapies to patients.


In this role, you will partner closely with project management, sponsors, CRAs, and cross-functional teams to drive study performance, oversee monitoring strategies, and ensure sites are supported from qualification through closeout. You will also serve as a key point of contact for sponsors and study teams, providing strategic oversight, mentoring site management teams, and ensuring clinical operations remain aligned with study goals, timelines, and quality expectations.


Where You'll Work


This is a remote role open to candidates based in Europe. You will collaborate with global teams across multiple time zones.


Travel will be required on an as-needed basis.


What You'll Do


  • Lead and coordinate clinical site management activities from study startup through database lock and study closeout.
  • Partner with project management to develop monitoring strategies, establish site management targets, and ensure delivery against project goals.
  • Provide leadership, guidance, and oversight to CRAs and site management team members across assigned studies and regions.
  • Serve as the primary site management representative for sponsors, study teams, investigator meetings, audits, inspections, and key project discussions.
  • Drive quality and compliance by overseeing monitoring activities, reviewing protocol deviations, ensuring adherence to Clinical Monitoring Plans, and maintaining inspection readiness.
  • Monitor study metrics, recruitment performance, resource allocation, and operational trends to identify risks and implement effective solutions.
  • Support patient recruitment efforts by tracking enrollment progress and guiding site-specific recruitment strategies to maintain study targets.
  • Ensure Trial Master File compliance and oversee the timely completion and quality review of site management documentation.
  • Proactively identify, escalate, and mitigate operational and monitoring risks while supporting issue resolution and continuous improvement initiatives.

What You'll Bring

  • Minimum 2 years relevant experience as a CTM/LCRA (or equivalent) including overseeing a CTM team.
  • Experience working with Oncology studies is required for this role.
  • Experience leading or coordinating clinical monitoring and site management activities within clinical trials.
  • Strong understanding of clinical research principles, site management processes, and monitoring best practices.
  • Knowledge of FDA and/or EU regulations, ICH Guidelines, local regulatory requirements, and clinical trial SOPs.
  • Experience reviewing study metrics, managing operational risks, supporting recruitment activities, and maintaining high-quality study documentation.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and clinical systems including EDC, CTMS, IxRS/IVRS, and eCRF platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and motivate remote teams, influence stakeholders, solve complex problems, and manage multiple priorities effectively.
  • Proficiency in English, with excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.

About Us:

Endpoint is an interactive response technology (IRT®) systems and solutions provider that supports the life sciences industry. Since 2009, we have been working with a single vision in mind, to help sponsors and pharmaceutical companies achieve clinical trial success. Endpoint Clinical is a trusted clinical trial technology and service partner delivering reliable randomization and trial supply management solutions. We are expanding our capabilities to bring clinical supply planning closer to real time trial execution, helping sponsors make better supply decisions with greater speed, confidence, and control. We are seeking an entrepreneurial executive to build and lead a clinical supply consulting and advisory practice focused on forecasting, planning, optimization, and intelligent decision support. This leader will combine deep clinical supply expertise with consulting discipline, executive presence, and commercial acumen.

The Opportunity

    This role sits at the intersection of clinical supply strategy, forecasting and optimization, RTSM/IRT, consulting services, product innovation, and commercial growth. You will serve as Endpoint's executive subject matter expert for clinical supply and help define how sponsors use data, technology, and practical expertise to improve decisions across the trial lifecycle. This is not a traditional clinical supply operations role. It is a build-and-lead opportunity for someone who can create repeatable advisory offerings, engage senior sponsor stakeholders, shape software capabilities, and establish a differentiated market position.

    • Build and lead the consulting practice
      • Establish and scale a clinical supply consulting and advisory capability.
      • Develop repeatable offerings, methodologies, frameworks, delivery standards, and intellectual property.

        • Guide customers through forecasting, manufacturing scenarios, inventory strategy, depot planning, overage, risk mitigation, and protocol-change impacts.
        • Facilitate executive discussions that convert uncertainty and complex data into clear decisions and actions.
        • Support strategic customer engagements, governance meetings, and business reviews.
        • Connect clinical supply planning with RTSM execution
          • Help customers use planning assumptions and real-time trial information to improve supply decisions.
          • Identify opportunities to reduce waste, improve responsiveness, and protect patient service levels.
          • Bring deep practical knowledge of RTSM/IRT workflows, integrations, and clinical supply operating models.
          • Shape product strategy and innovation
            • Collaborate with Product, Technology, Commercial, and Delivery leaders to translate market needs into scalable capabilities.
            • Use consulting insights to inform product priorities, workflow design, analytics, and decision-support use cases.
            • Act as a voice of the customer in the evolution of Endpoint clinical supply intelligence solutions.
            • Driving commercial growth and industry leadership
              • Participate in strategic pursuits, executive briefings, proposals, and solution design.
              • Create consulting-led entry points and expansion opportunities within sponsor organizations.
              • Represent Endpoint at industry events and build a credible external point of view through speaking and thought leadership.

What you will bring

    • 15+ years of experience in clinical trial supply management, clinical supply strategy, supply-chain consulting, clinical operations, or a closely related discipline.
    • Deep understanding of global clinical supply planning and execution, including forecasting, packaging and labeling, manufacturing constraints, inventory, distribution, depots, comparators, returns, and supply risk.
    • Strong working knowledge of RTSM/IRT and the relationship between supply planning and live study execution.
    • Experience advising pharmaceutical or biotechnology organizations on complex operational and strategic decisions.
    • Demonstrated ability to build methodologies, offerings, teams, or new business capabilities.
    • Credibility and confidence with senior executives and cross-functional stakeholders.
    • Commercial judgment, including the ability to identify needs, shape solutions, support proposals, and create measurable value.
    • Excellent communication, facilitation, writing, and presentation skills.
    • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience. An advanced degree or relevant professional certification

Leadership Profile

    • Entrepreneurial and comfortable building from an early foundation.
    • Customer-centered, outcome-oriented, and practical.
    • Analytical, data-driven, and able to simplify complex decisions.
    • Collaborative across product, technology, commercial, and delivery teams.
    • Visible and credible as an industry leader, while remaining hands-on when needed.
    • Committed to quality, speed, agility, and strong customer partnerships.

What Success looks like
